X.note: The rich weathered stone with waterline staining is the most convincing material of the three. The geometry is broken, though. Dark wedge-shaped holes and gaps cut into the wall face, there are visible white edge seams and a dotted artifact at the lower right, and the terrace texture is smeared. It looks like a scanned or photogrammetry mesh with holes. The surrounding buildings are untextured grey boxes. The flat grey tarmac-like road reads as modern.

Y.note: This is the cleanest and most coherent render. The pale limestone walls are plausible, with slit openings and a gravel terrace. The parapet blocks look chunky and toy-like. The terrace has a pale paved or kerb strip along the road that looks modern. The background blocks are still untextured grey boxes, and the road is smooth tarmac. There is no flicker.

Z.note: The walls are smooth, pale, near-featureless slabs with very little stone detail. The dark terrace looks like fresh asphalt or carpet. The result is clean but sterile, like a CG mock-up or architectural massing model. The road kerb strip and the grey box buildings add to the modern feel.

why: Y has a clean, intact, believable stone bastion with a gravel terrace and no render defects, whereas X has the best material richness but visible holes and seam artifacts, and Z is sterile, featureless and asphalt-like.
anachronisms_seen: smooth grey tarmac-like road around the bastion
kerb or paved strip along the road edge
uniform pale clean masonry that looks newly cut rather than 1782 weathered limestone (Y, Z)
